segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was to do or to make?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We said that for the informal positive command, we have a shortcut. We find the you version of the verb, haces, and we take away the s, hace.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: But with hacer, we have an irregularity. The informal command from hacer is haz, H-A-Z. So in most of Spain, you will hear haz, haz.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you want to say, "Do it"...

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another use of the mood tense is to turn words like "where" into "wherever". What was "where"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So of course we can't use the mood tense with dónde because it's not a verb. How would you say "where you want", "where you want", speaking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now if we want to say "wherever you want", then to get "wherever", actually we can change the verb to the mood tense, and that changes the feeling of "where", and then "where" turns into "wherever". So if you want to say "wherever you want", still informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: I want to hear well the i and the e in quieras.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Donde quieras. So, "Do it wherever you want."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Hazlo donde quieras. What was "you like it", still informally, "you like it"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: How would you say "do it how you like to do it", so "do it how you like"? What was the word for "how"? "How are you called?", "What's your name?"

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Cómo. Good. So do it how it pleases you, "do it how you like".

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Hazlo como te gusta. Do it how you like to, do it how you like to do it.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now what if you wanted to give the meaning "do it however you like"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hazlo como te guste. In English, we are changing "how" to "however", and in Spanish, we are changing te gusta to te guste.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Hazlo como te guste. How would you say "do what you prefer", "do what you prefer", still informal?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Haz lo que prefieres.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So what we are investigating here is an optional use of the mood tense, no? Because haz lo que prefieres is perfect Spanish, it just means "do what you prefer". But if you want to give the meaning "do whatever you prefer", how will you change that?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Haz lo que prefieras. "Do whatever you prefer." "Eat whatever you prefer", "eat whatever you prefer", speaking informally.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Comes lo que prefieras would be "you eat whatever you prefer", comes lo que prefieras, which is a way of saying it, you could say it like this, comes lo que prefieras, it just sounds actually a little sweeter, "you eat whatever you prefer", ah, rather than "eat whatever you prefer". But here we're working with the order.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We have a shortcut where we're not using the mood tense, what is it? We have comes, "you eat", and what do we do to get the order?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So making the order, even though your sentence was very nice and very sweet, comes lo que prefieras, let's make it an order. "Eat whatever you prefer."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Come lo que prefieras.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Now make this formal: "Eat whatever you prefer", but speaking formally.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. So here we have two mood tenses: we have coma, which is the order, and then prefiera, giving us "whatever" from "what". Coma lo que prefiera. What if you were speaking to more than one person? "Eat whatever you prefer."

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Good. Coman lo que prefieran. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What was "to need" in Spanish, sounding more like "to necessitate"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Whenever you need", "whenever you need", how do you say that, speaking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Cuando necesites. "Whenever you need." Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: We said that "to choose" was like "elect", elegir, elegir. How would you say "I choose"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And we had some change happening with that e.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Elijo. Good. Elijo. "You choose", speaking informally?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "To follow", and also "to continue" or "to carry on", we can use this verb like that, is seguir, seguir. So it's to follow or to continue, to carry on, seguir.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And this behaves like elegir in that the e will not split, it will just turn into an i when we stress it. So how do you say "I continue" or "I follow"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And there are some other verbs that come from seguir: we have conseguir, "to get" or "to manage to"; we have perseguir, which means "to chase", and we will see the same irregularity in them. The I version of conseguir, consigo; perseguir, persigo. So, like we said before, we can generalize the irregularities in Spanish.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So sigo, "I follow", and how about "he", "she", "it follows", or "you" formal "follow"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Seguimos. Good. We're not stressing the e, so it escapes from the irregularity. Seguimos. Good.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So we could say something like "I'll follow you wherever you go". So we can say "I will follow you" or we can just use the present, "I follow you", because the "wherever you go" is a future context, informally.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Wherever you go". So this is actually "to wherever you go", "wherever you go to", "to wherever you go". So how would you say "to where"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Adónde. Good. And "you go", informally, and we want the mood tense, which is irregular?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Yes, very good. So now we can say the whole sentence: "I'll follow you wherever you go", "to wherever you go", informally.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Another irregular verb in the mood tense is ser. The base for the mood tense of ser is sea, sea, S-E-A.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: And you will hear the very common expression o sea, o sea, literally meaning something like "or it might be". O sea, o sea is just like this kind of way to break up speech whilst you're thinking what to say, like an "er". So sea is the base for the mood tense.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So if you want to say something like "I prefer that it be like this", "I prefer that it's like this", "I prefer for it to be like this", of course we say "I prefer that it be like this". What was the word for "like this" or "like that"?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: So "I prefer that it be like this", "I prefer it to be like this".

segments.speaker: Student
segments.text: Prefiero que lo... Do we... No, we don't need lo here. Prefiero que sea así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: Very good. Prefiero que sea así.

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: What does sea lo que sea mean?

segments.speaker: Teacher
segments.text: "Whatever it is", "whatever will be, will be", sea lo que sea, "whatever will come". Good.
